title: Hosted-to-Dedicated Cutover Simulation — agenda + slide skeleton
objectives: Validate cutover choreography for moving a production route from hosted API -> dedicated pool with simulated traffic
Exercise and timebox fallback paths (model-variant fallback, region fallback, degrade-to-simulated-response) and verify SLAs
Verify observability: key dashboards, alert triggers, and automated rollback conditions
Surface ops/permission gaps and pre-cutover runbook tasks that must be completed before a customer migration window
prework_for_customer: Provide a short list of production routes (2-3) to include in simulation + expected QPS and 95/99 latency targets
Confirm service account + IP allowlist for dedicated pool access (or KMS details for Private)
Export recent 72h traffic profile (percentiles, typical seq lengths) as CSV
Install Redwood smoke-test harness (step script supplied) in customer staging environment
agenda_items: 00:00-00:10 — Welcome, goals, success criteria (host + cust leads)
00:10-00:25 — Architecture recap: hosted routing + dedicated pool topology (slide 1-3)
00:25-00:45 — Simulation plan walk-through: traffic generator, gradual ramp, canary percentages (slide 4-6)
00:45-01:20 — Live simulation round 1: ramp to 10% traffic, observe metrics, validate cache warmup
01:20-01:35 — Pause + retro: anomalies, dashboards, on-call actions
01:35-02:05 — Live simulation round 2: increase to 50% with model variant fallback enabled
02:05-02:20 — Inject failure scenario: GPU OOM on dedicated node -> automatic fallback verification
02:20-02:35 — Rollback drill: execute rollback play, confirm traffic back to hosted, verify metrics
02:35-02:55 — After-action review: open issues, decision log, outstanding pre-cutover tasks
02:55-03:00 — Next steps, responsibilities, and scheduling formal cutover window

Slide 1: Motivations and expected business outcomes (cost, latency, isolation)

facilitator_notes: Start by confirming success criteria verbally and capture in the doc — align on 'what good looks like'
Keep timebox strict for live simulation segments; call for pause at the 30s/1min mark if dashboards are unstable
Remind customer engineers to avoid unrelated config changes during simulation — use 'simulation' branch rules
When injecting failure, announce intent 1 minute prior and confirm rollback owner is ready
If traffic generator cannot reproduce seq-length distribution, note as action item and proceed with percentile-based validation
If alerts fire, capture full alert payload and Slack thread link for postmortem; do not immediately silence without triage
Use simple language for non-technical stakeholders; provide short blurbs on each slide summarizing "why" behind each decision
roles_and_responsibilities: Customer tech lead — approves test routes, owns rollback decision for their traffic
SE lead (Miguel) — facilitator, runs simulation plan and controls traffic generator
SRE on-call (Samir) — monitors infra metrics, executes node-level remediation if needed
Platform engineer (Lina) — ensures dedicated pool config, secrets, and routing policies are correct
Product PM (Priya) — observes SLA impacts and notes product-level acceptance criteria
metrics_to_watch: End-to-end P95 latency (hosted vs dedicated) — immediate comparator
Request error rate (5m rolling) — spike during ramp indicates capacity or model issues
GPU utilization and queue depth on dedicated nodes
Model token generation rate and KV cache hit ratio
Ingress QPS and backend p99 tail latencies
rollback_criteria: Sustained p95 latency > 2x baseline for > 5 minutes
Error rate increase > 1% absolute for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows
Dedicated pool node OOMs or repeated preemption events
Traffic routing automation fails to revert within the configured timeout
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Cache cold-start causes initial latency spike — Mitigation: pre-warm prefix cache using recorded traffic tracers
Risk: Secret/KMS permission missing in dedicated environment — Mitigation: verify IAM bindings pre-sim and run a credential smoke test
Risk: Observability gaps — Mitigation: enable temporary high-frequency metrics and distributed tracing for the simulation window
Risk: Customer infra changes during sim — Mitigation: lock-change window and require PR approvals during run
required_materials_and_tools: Access to Redwood Console dashboards and per-route traces
Smoke-test scripts (appendix CLI commands) and sample payloads
Slack channel for play-by-play and escalation (#cust-cutover-sim)
open_questions_and_followups: Can customer provide a 7-day token distribution sample (we only have 72h) — action: customer to upload by 2025-11-10
Confirm final DNS TTL and expected propagation time for cutover window — action: Lina to verify with infra ops
Decide on canary step sizes beyond 50% (customer preference) — action: product + customer to decide after sim
Add automated post-cutover regression checks to the release pipeline (linked PR above)
success_criteria_for_simulation: Traffic routed to dedicated pool at target canary percentages with stable latencies within SLA
Fallback paths triggered and reverted as expected during failure injection
No missing permissions or configuration blockers remain in the pre-cutover checklist
All action items assigned with owners and dates; cutover window scheduled
post_sim_follow_up_actions: Capture a decision log and attach recordings + console snapshots to the Confluence DEP-1234 page
Fill gaps in pre-cutover checklist and re-run smoke-tests in staging within 48 hours
Schedule formal cutover with customer OPS, include 2-hour dry-run during low traffic window
Create pager runbook snippet for Week-0 post-cutover monitoring and assign SRE rotations
